name: Bow Falls
text: [approach] From the Bow Glacier lot the falls are in view to the southwest.

name: Gorby Falls
text: [approach] These flows hang a short way to the right of Bow Falls, so walk the Bow Falls approach from the Bow Glacier lot (lake edge, or across the frozen lake, to the moraine) and continue to the right.

name: Left compound gully
peak: Compound Gullies at Waterton Wardens compound
text: [overview] the icefalls show on the right while driving into Waterton townsite.
[overview] Walk up in 30 to 45 minutes, depending on pace and snow depth.
[approach] The walk is short but steep, and takes longer in deep snow.

name: Right compound gully
peak: Compound Gullies at Waterton Wardens compound
text: [overview] Its WI3 first pitch, about 70 m, is the most striking icefall visible from the road;
[overview] Above it, a lengthy and easy snow pitch leads to an upper icefall of perhaps 30 m, which was not climbed in warm conditions.
[overview] Listed as 5 pitches although only 2 were climbed, since the snow might be split into pitches if it were ice.
[approach] The walk is short but takes longer in deep snow.

name: No nuts no glory
text: [overview] From the southeast shore of Lake Agnes, head up steep, avalanche-prone snow on the climber's left side of the wall to an overhanging yellow cave.
[overview] P5 is 30 m of steep snow, about 60 degrees, angling left to a tree;

name: Coire Dubh Integrale
text: [overview] Finishing on Loder Peak, this line has winter ice, plus snowy ground and rock.
[overview] Snow depth decides how hard that pitch is.

name: Asteroid Alley
text: [approach] Walk up the glacier-tour road until it drops toward the ice, then follow an occasionally cairned trail up toward the prominent gully you can see from the lot, just below the icefall.
[approach] Stay low enough to keep off the glacier but high enough to avoid losing elevation.

name: Southwest Ridge
text: [beta] Above the tarns, cross a faint headwall right to left, follow the glacial stream to a shallow col, and cross the snowy plateau to the ridge.
[hazards] Snow slope needing axe and crampons.
[hazards] Glacier and snowfield travel.
[gear] Ice axe.
[gear] Crampons.
[turnaround] Turn back if the notches are wet or icy or the snow slope is too hard without crampons.
[pitch_detail] Snow.
[pitch_detail] Faint route across the headwall to a col and snowy plateau;
[pitch_detail] ice axe and crampons for the snow slope..

name: East Ridge
text: [overview] Graded 5.3 with moderate snow.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — if the route holds snow or ice
[approach] A snow couloir flanks the ridge on one side and the north face on the other.

name: Riptide
text: [overview] Riptide descends from the Snowbird Glacier.
[overview] Ice is often hollow, brittle, thin and plastered with snow;
[approach] Several hundred feet of steep snow lead to the base, where you dig out a belay platform.

name: Aemmer Couloir
text: [overview] A cornice is often present;
[approach] The couloir steepens and narrows as you climb and a cornice often sits at the top.

[approach] The approach crosses avalanche terrain and passes under glacier and serac hazard from the north face, so check the avalanche forecast, and ask Parks Canada about any current trail restrictions.

name: Greenwood-Jones
text: [overview] A limestone pitch tops the buttress and a corniced ridge follows.
[descent_text] From the top of the buttress, slog loose scree on the glacier's left side to the crest of the ridge, where the East Ridge route arrives above the Black Towers.
[descent_text] Continue along the corniced summit ridge to the top, then descend the easy southwest slopes to Moraine Lake.

name: Squashed Bones
text: [overview] From the top, traverse leftward (south) along ledges, over snow or loose scree, to the East Ridge under the Black Towers, then roughly 6 further rope-length pitches, of 5th class difficulty, easier to middling, with bolted belays, lead up to the ice cap crowni
[what_to_bring] crampons and an ice tool — the ice cap on the summit

name: East Face
text: [overview] Place belays carefully, avoid the route if snow lies on the ledges, and note that a large ledge cuts across the whole face and offers an escape prior to the serious difficulties.

name: This House of Sky
text: [overview] Moderate ice rambles on endlessly, one short WI3 icefall after another.

name: French kiss
text: [approach] French Kiss is the first obvious icefall on the right as you head toward the lake, and the left-most flow in the amphitheatre.

name: Cobre Verde
text: [overview] The gully above has a handful of brief ice steps and wandering pitches, but deep snow often discourages going higher.

name: Dawn of the Dead
text: [approach] Start at the Stanley Glacier trailhead on Highway 93 South in Kootenay National Park and follow the signed switchbacking trail up through the trees until it opens into the upper valley, with the headwall rising on the right.
[approach] Skis or snowshoes are usual in winter.
